title.narrative: NESsT - Strengthening green and equitable social enterprises
NESsT - Stärka gröna och rättvisa sociala företag

description.narrative:
The overall goal and expected results of the intervention: is to invest in 20 green value chain and circular economy enterprises in Brazil, Colombia, and Peru to create and sustain at least 2,000 jobs, generate local economic growth, and protect the environment while also increasing equity and inclusion for marginalized populations such as women and Indigenous Peoples. An important added value of this intervention is the possibility for these enterprises to join global value chain markets of bigger corporations such as IKEA.
For achieving this goal, five specific objectives have been drawn up:
1. Strengthen the business and operational capacity of 15 social enterprises (within the green value chain sector) so they increase sales, commercial partnerships, sustainable supply chain management, and achieve client diversification and investment-readiness.
2. Mitigate climate change by training green value chain and circular economy enterprises to integrate an environmental and climate change perspective and sustainable supply chain management.
3. Prioritize gender equity and inclusion within the social enterprises
4. Engage corporations to improve and diversify supply chains
5. Capture the learnings to share with the larger sector
NESst is a new partner to Sida but has ample experience of working accelerating and funding high-impact social enterprises that create viable income opportunities for underserved communities while contributing positively to climate change mitigation and gender equality.
Their activities are relevant for the Swedish Strategy for regional development cooperation with Latin America and are in line the new reform agenda for the international cooperation.

Detta är ett stöd till NESst i ett projekt som heter "Stärka gröna och rättvisa sociala företag i Sydamerika" under perioden 1 juni 2024 till 31 maj 2027. Den totala budgeten för projektet är SEK 12 000 000. The Nonprofit Enterprise Self-Sustaininability Team (NeSst) kommer att komplettera Sidas bidrag med 900. 000 USD från IKEA Social Entrepreneurship, vilket ger en total budget för projektet på nära 2 miljoner USD.
Det övergripande målet och de förväntade resultaten av insatsen är att investera i 15 företag inom gröna värdekedjor och cirkulär ekonomi i Brasilien, Colombia och Peru för att skapa minst 1 500 långsiktiga arbetstillfällen, stimulera lokal ekonomisk tillväxt och skydda miljön samtidigt som det främjar jämställdhet och inkludering av marginaliserade befolkningar som kvinnor och ursprungsbefolkningar. Ett viktigt mervärde med denna insats är att dessa företag får möjlighet att ansluta sig till globala värdekedjor hos större företag som IKEA.
För att uppnå det övergripande målet har fem specifika mål formulerats:
1. Stärka affärs- och verksamhetskapaciteten hos 15 sociala företag inom sektorn för global gröna värdekedjor för att uppnå ökad försäljning, nya handelsrelationer, hållbar hantering av leveranskedjor, diversifierad kundbas och större beredskap att göra investeringar.
2. Mildra effekter av klimatförändringar genom att utbilda företag inom gröna värdekedjor och cirkulär ekonomi för att integrera ett miljö- och klimatperspektiv samt hållbara försörjningskedjor.
3. Prioritera jämställdhet och integration inom de sociala företagen.
4. Engagera företag för förbättrade och diversifierade leveranskedjor.
5. Fånga lärdomar och dela dessa med den större sektorn.
NESst är en ny partner till Sida men har stor erfarenhet av att arbeta med att påskynda och finansiera sociala företag med stor genomslagskraft som skapar livskraftiga inkomstmöjligheter för underprivilegierade samhällen samtidigt som de bidrar positivt till begränsning av klimatförändringar och jämställdhet.
Deras verksamhet är relevant för den svenska strategin för regionalt utvecklingssamarbete med Latinamerika och ligger i linje med den nya reformagendan för det internationella samarbetet.
Team Sweden-kategori: B: Sektor: Fred och landsbygdsutveckling, land: Colombia

This is a support to NESst in a project called "Strengthening green and equitable social enterprises in South America". NESsT will match SIDA’s investment with IKEA Social Entrepreneurship. The overall goal and expected results of the intervention: is to invest in 20 green value chain and circular economy enterprises in Brazil, Colombia, and Peru to create and sustain at least 2000 jobs, generate local economic growth, and protect the environment while also increasing equity and inclusion for marginalized populations such as women and Indigenous Peoples. An important added value of this intervention is the possibility for these enterprises to join global value chain markets of bigger corporations such as IKEA.
To achieve the overall goal, five specific goal formulations have:
1. Strengthen the business and operational capacity of 15 social enterprises in the global green value chain sector to increase sales, new trade relationships, sustainable supply chain management, diversified customer base and greater readiness to make investments.
2. Mitigate effects of climate change by training companies in green value chains and circular economy to integrate an environmental and climate perspective as well as sustainable supply chains.
3. Prioritize equality and integration within the social enterprises.
4. Engage companies for improved and diversified supply chains.
5. Capture lessons learned and share these with the wider sector.
NESst is a new partner to Sida but has extensive experience in working with accelerating and financing high-impact social enterprises that create viable income opportunities for underprivileged communities while contributing positively to climate change mitigation and gender equality.
Their activities are relevant to the Swedish strategy for regional development cooperation with Latin America and are in line with the new reform agenda for international cooperation.

title.narrative: Signed Agreement Sida - NESsT Strengthening green and equitable social enterprises

description.narrative:
NESsT has been a partner to Sida since 2024. It has started as a regional contribution benefiting 15 social enterprises in Brazil, Peru and Colombia (5 in each country). Later that year, a major amendment was made to include a component to benefit 5 more social enterprises in Colombia. The two cooperation teams complement each other and follow-up this contribution jointly. In accordance with the partners June 2024- May 2025 annual report, the key results achieved through the contribution are outlined below:
Regional component:
The narrative report presents a comprehensive analysis of each of the 15 social enterprise that is part of the regional portfolio, including the main progresses they made during the year, challenges and lessons learned. The report was accompanied by 5 annexes in which NESsT details the specific actions taken with each enterprise in the regional portfolio (considering that the enterprises in the bilateral were being selected during the first year of the reporting), then an annex on the communication strategy (posts and its impact) and finally, an annex with NESsTs Performance Monitoring Tool (PMT) measuring impact indicators of each supported enterprise.
During the first year of the project, key insights on investment readiness and enterprise resilience were generated. At the regional level, the partner has supported 15 enterprises. 14 enterprises were evaluated for Due Diligence, 2,041 jobs created (42% women), USD 5.16 million in revenues generated with 8% profitability, and multiple climate and gender initiatives were carried out. The program demonstrably enhanced the investment readiness of participating social enterprises. Key achievements include:
- Improved Financial Management: Several enterprises received targeted assistance to strengthen their financial management. For example, in Brazil, NESsT supported Plantus in improving record-keeping using the Conta Azul system, focusing on cost control and sales reporting. In Peru, Orígenes (CAOVL) received specialized financial mentoring and developed cash flow tools. These interventions are critical for attracting future investment.
- Climate Resilience Initiatives: In Brazil, the program supported climate resilience initiatives. The reforestation initiative with Assoab and the solar energy project with Coopersapó are directly addressing climate change vulnerabilities. NESsT is monitoring these initiatives closely to assess the potential for scaling similar efforts across the cohort. Several enterprises implemented tangible climate resilience and environmental practices. In Brazil, Assoab planted 3,000 Brazil nut seedlings across 30 hectares to restore degraded land, while Coopersapó designed a solar energy project to overcome drought-related processing challenges. In Colombia, Agrosolidaria protected 2,600 hectares of Amazonian forest while expanding the commercialization of native species. In Peru, AFIMAD successfully diversified into Muru Muru production, generating cash flow while reducing deforestation pressures. Together, portfolio enterprises managed over 1 million hectares of land and advanced regenerative practices that directly address climate risks.
- Training & Integration: the inclusion of environmental and climate change perspectives as part of NESsT's support indicates a commitment to building this capacity within the enterprises. In Brazil, the NESsT team developed customized priorities and action plans with the five SEs, also aiming to strengthen gender and environmental practices.
- Job Creation for Women: Enterprises such as Maré de Sabores in Brazil directly trained and supported low-income women to build businesses, while Coopersapó empowered its female members through initiatives like a women-led collective kitchen. These efforts show measurable progress but also highlight the need to ensure that women not only access jobs but also equitable income distributioncurrently only 28% of supplier revenues go to women.
- Setting Gender Priorities: Gender-focused actions were integrated across all SEs, reinforcing NESsT's commitment to gender equity and inclusion. These priorities were embedded in annual planning and tailored to each enterprise's needs. In Brazil NESsT facilitated training on sustainable practices with a gender perspective across the entire portfolio, aiming to include as many women as possible. The goal is to enhance women's technical skills and increase their formal participation in associations and cooperatives.
The program started to make connections for engaging corporations. The NESsT team is actively fostering connections among the SEs and between SEs and corporate partners with the support of Sida which has made the connection with Business Sweden in the Embassies of Colombia and Brazil and is planning to organize one for the supported enterprises in Peru.
Bilateral component:
The report clearly shows the rigorous selection process used to identify the five companies supported by Colombia's bilateral program. Working with companies that have received support from other partners adds value to this program because it builds on previous support. Additionally, we ensure that we reach target populations in conflict-affected areas, most of whom are victims. Therefore, the Embassy closely monitored this process.
The embassy appreciates NESsT's willingness to engage in dialogue with other Swedish partners and its capacity to adjust timelines and activities to the new selection process. NESsT also viewed this collaboration as a positive learning experience for developing a high-quality pipeline. If the program receives additional funding from Sweden or other donors, it would be beneficial to expand the number of partners for future cohorts.
The Embassy also valued the due diligence process carried out on the 14 initiatives that applied. This process resulted in the selection of the five best initiatives.
1. Aprocasur in Bolívar; 2. Ecoserrania in Antioquia, which was previously supported by Fondo Acción;
3. Coopitayó in Cauca, which is supported by FAO;
4. Coagropacifico in Tumaco, Nariño; and 5. Selva Nevada, previous winners of Emprender Paz.
We agree with NESsT that their evaluation mechanisms and processeswhich combine quantitative and qualitative variables and toolsresult in a rigorous selection process.
The report provides a detailed overview of the steps developed in the due diligence process. Stage 1: Technical Evaluation Using a Scoring Matrix Five members of the NESsT team assessed each application independently to ensure diverse perspectives and prioritize technical merit. Stage 2: In-Depth Interviews, Capacity Assessment, and Internal Selection Committee: This stage aimed to complement the quantitative results with a qualitative understanding of the business model, governance, impact traceability, and institutional capacity. Stage 3: Internal Selection Committee with the Embassy's participation.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
